target_customer: African small and mid-sized businesses and growing companies hiring across African countries
problem: Kenyan employers' payroll systems had not kept up with mobile money, and SMBs lacked a mobile-first HR and payroll product. Workpay offers payroll software and outsourcing, Employer of Record, compliance, benefits and salary disbursement across Africa.
business_model: SaaS subscription per employee plus payroll outsourcing, Employer of Record and disbursement fees
product_category: HR, payroll and Employer of Record platform for Africa

founders.name: Paul Kimani
education: Electrical and Electronic Engineering, University of Nairobi
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Google for Startups Africa alumnus and eFounders Fellowship by UNCTAD and Alibaba Group.

founders.name: Jackson Kibigo Kungu
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2024-08-22) names Jackson Kungu co-founder and COO; Techpoint (2020-08-14) names Jackson Kibigo as co-founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payroll with country-specific statutory rules, mobile money and bank disbursement integrations is standard SaaS with compliance-heavy hard parts that multiply per country.

defensibility.rationale: Payroll data and statutory compliance know-how across many African countries are costly to rebuild, and payroll is sticky, but global players such as Deel and Rippling can enter.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch (2024) names global rivals Rippling, Gusto and Deel (which bought PaySpace) and local SeamlessHR, PaidHR and Bento; none acquired Workpay.

market_need_then: Kenyan SMBs lacked mobile-first payroll in 2020 and in the Google startup story Kimani says no such SMB subscription product existed. At the August 2020 seed it served more than 250 SMBs paying over 20,000 employees monthly.

branding.name_origin: Renamed from TozzaPlus to WorkPay in June 2019 when the team narrowed from ERP to HR and payroll; no source states why the new name was chosen.
branding.domain_note: Uses myworkpay.com rather than workpay.com, suggesting the exact .com was not obtained; no purchase history found.

identity.visual_style: Corporate SaaS site with awards and customer logos

rebrands.why: Team narrowed from a broad ERP suite to HR and payroll; rename followed the pivot (Techpoint).

branding.community_and_virality: Company lists awards such as Best HR and Payroll Software in Kenya (2022, 2023) and Africa (2022); these are self-reported.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear descriptive name that dropped the confusing TozzaPlus, backed by regional awards, but no evidence of community or viral spread and the .com is a variant.

pivots.from: TozzaPlus, a full ERP software suite
pivots.to: HR and payroll software, renamed WorkPay in June 2019
pivots.why: Narrowed to HR management after early traction in HR software (over 200 B2B clients in 2018 to 2019 per Techpoint).

outcome_analysis: Workpay pivoted from an ERP to mobile-first payroll in 2018 and 2019, entered YC Winter 2020 and raised a $2.1M seed led by Kepple Africa. It then added a $2.7M round in 2023 and a $5M Series A in August 2024 led by Norrsken22 with Visa, reaching about 130 staff and an Employer of Record business across 50 plus African countries. It is active with nearly $10M raised.
notes: Founding year is 2017 as TozzaPlus per Techpoint; YC and the company site say 2019. Recorded rounds total about $9.95M against TechCrunch's nearly $10M, so coverage is marked complete; a Launch Africa headline mentioning $8.8M was not opened. The 2023 round is labeled other because sources call it pre-seed in one outlet (The Star) and pre-Series A in TechCrunch. Competitors: directory sites list SeamlessHR, PaidHR and others but undated; SeamlessHR's first reported round was a $10M Series A in January 2022, and TechCrunch's rival list is from 2024, so no competitor with a source dated near the 2020 batch was found and the list is empty. Jackson's surname appears as Kibigo and Kungu. YC page lists him only as Founder.
